thread:
maria_support: acme_ops flagged a subtle brevity/tonality change after the rdx-1.4.2 rollout this morning. They attached short before/after snippets — can eng triage?

acme_ops: Noticed the shift ~2026-03-15 09:18 UTC when we started hitting rdx-1.4.2. Before: 'Thanks for reaching out — I can help walk you through resetting your password and checking account settings.' After: 'I can help. Reset password steps:' Fewer tokens, less hedging. We're on hosted API, model=rdx-1.4.2, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95. Pasting minimal repro below.

maria_support: can you paste a curl repro and the two raw responses (before/after) so we can compare token counts? Also confirm whether you set a custom system prompt.

acme_ops: repro (we saved pre-upgrade logs and current):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rdx-1.4.2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"How do I reset my password?"}],"temperature":0.2}'
```
BEFORE (rdx-1.4.1): "Thanks for reaching out — I can help. To reset your password, go to Settings > Security, click Reset, and follow the emailed link. If you run into issues, let me know and I can assist further." (approx 43 tokens)
AFTER (rdx-1.4.2): "I can help. To reset your password, go to Settings > Security > Reset. Follow the emailed link." (approx 18 tokens)

charlie_sre: I'm looking at the rollout. Release notes indicate a default flip: ff/compact-output was enabled for rdx-1.4.2 on hosted pools to save tokens. Checking flags for tenant scope.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: release rdx-1.4.2 deployed 2026-03-15T09:17:36Z by pipeline/main; feature flips applied: ff/compact-output=true (env=hosted, rollout=global)

eli_ml: We also introduced a small generation objective tweak (avg token penalty +0.05) to reduce padding in conversational responses. That change was intended for opt-in beta but looks like the compact-output flag plus the penalty ended up enabled for hosted by default. This explains the shorter, more direct style — not a semantic understanding regression but a generation objective shift.

dana_product: We need a quick mitigation and rollback plan. Maria, can support offer a workaround while we revert the default? And Eng, please scope how long to revert and add tests to prevent accidental global flips.

maria_support: acme_ops — temporary workarounds you can apply now: 1) pin model to rdx-1.4.1 (model=rdx-1.4.1) OR 2) send request header `x-output-verbosity: verbose` (per-request) OR 3) set `generation_params.verbosity = "verbose"` in the body. Sorry about the surprise; engineering is on it.

acme_ops: quick Q — can we set the header per route in our proxy? we use a gateway that injects headers automatically.

charlie_sre: Yes, the serving runtime accepts the `x-output-verbosity` header per request. We've validated the header overrides the ff/compact-output default. Example: `-H "x-output-verbosity: verbose"`. Also `generation_params.verbosity` in the payload works.

acme_ops: Tried the header — responses look back to normal length and tone. Thanks for the fast workaround :rocket:

maria_support: marking this thread resolved for the customer side. Eng will revert the default flip for hosted and add a test to prevent non-gated tuning changes from going live globally. I'll follow up with postmortem once rolling revert ETA is set.

eli_ml: action items for ML: revert the default objective tweak in hosted, move compact-output behind tenant opt-in, add a regression eval comparing token length and politeness metrics on representative prompts.

dana_product: noted. I'll open an internal ticket and prioritize rollback this sprint.

maria_support: thanks all — keeping this thread here for audit; will attach postmortem and customer follow-up when available.
